notes:
Account background: enterprise fintech (trading signals + real-time chat). POC run Jun->Sep 2025. Redwood team: AE Anika Shah, SE Jordan Kim. Target: p95 <= 250ms for short-turn chat (<=128 tokens) and streaming startup latency <100ms.

Timeline (high level):
- 2025-07-10: Intro call (use cases, legality, SSO/KMS requirements).
- 2025-08-04: Technical deep dive; agreed POC scope (Dedicated trial, sample traffic).
- 2025-09-01: POC cluster provisioned (4x A100 reserved).
- 2025-09-23: Mid-POC sync; sent telemetry collection (linked ff_2025-09-23_8423).
- 2025-10-01: Final POC run and perf report (p95 data uploaded drive://redwood/telemetry/axiom-p95-report-2025-10-01.csv, call ff_2025-10-01_1190).
- 2025-10-12: Last contact; legal flagged budget freeze and security questions. No response after this date.

Key technical findings from POC:
- Measured latency: median generation ~160-220ms, but p95 consistently 580-720ms for targets that should be <=250ms. Tail dominated by initial-token and streaming chunk startup.
- Streaming issues: client sees large first-chunk delay (~350-500ms) then bursty streaming; occasional reconnects under heavy session histories.
- Root causes identified by SE: combination of (1) KV cache misses on long conversational contexts, (2) server-side continuous batching + TLS handshake overhead for inbound connections, (3) cross-VPC hop between customer app and inference nodes adding jitter.
- Mitigations tried during POC: disable continuous batching/force small batch sizes (reduced throughput, tail still poor), reduce context window retention (improved p95 marginally but broke session continuity), switch to q4 quantized model (lower cost, introduced false positives on trade alerts), fallback to smaller model (p95 ~240ms but unacceptable quality).
- Dedicated hardware (4xA100) reduced median but not tail. Hypothesis: tail is systemic (network and streaming protocol) not just raw GPU compute.

Security/legal: SOC2 + data residency required. KMS integration looked OK in lab but legal requested HSM proof for production. Security team opened RDW-1192 and RDW-1228; outstanding answers slowed procurement.

Customer sentiment / quotes:
- CTO (Priya Menon): "If we can't hit 250ms p95 for short chat we can't migrate from legacy infra."
- Head of ML Ops: "Quality drop with quantization is a non-starter for alerts — false positives cost us money."

Commercial/organizational notes:
- Internal champion (lead PM) left team in Sept; no replacement identified — hit 'no_internal_champion' in deal.
- Budget freeze raised by procurement on 2025-10-12 (email thread 17543f2a9b8c:mail).
- Competitor motion: TitanServe running edge-nodes with closer network footprint pitched lower-latency demo; Axiom evaluating TitanServe for edge routing.

Current state: Stalled / effectively closed-lost on technical fit grounds (tail latency + streaming). Sales outreach attempted 2025-10-20 and 2025-11-05; unresponsive. Legal and security remain blockers; even if budget freed, technical SLO risk remains high.

Suggested internal follow-ups for Redwood:

- Propose an architecture trial: co-located inference (customer VPC peering) + TLS session pooling to remove handshake cost. Offer 2-week edge trial with strict SLA baseline.
- Capture learnings for product: streaming startup optimization (pre-send headers, warm TLS, persistent connections), KV cache warm strategies, and an official quantization-quality matrix for trading workloads.
